target_customer: R&D teams at pharma and biotech companies that screen and de-risk drug candidates
problem: Drug discovery is slow and expensive, and candidates fail late on safety and translation. CellType sells computational simulation of human biology to screen compounds, predict cross-species safety and forecast clinical translation earlier.
business_model: B2B enterprise software and platform deals with pharma, plus partnerships
product_category: AI drug discovery, biological foundation models and agents

founders.name: David van Dijk
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a Yale professor, built biological foundation models with Google and turned down Google to start CellType. Degrees not stated on the pages opened (PhD title only).

founders.name: Ivan Vrkic
prior_employers: CERN (software for the Large Hadron Collider)
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. School and degrees not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires biological foundation models (a 27B parameter model built on Gemma was reported, developed with Google DeepMind) plus agent pipelines validated against real biology. Research-grade for a team of two to five.

defensibility.rationale: Academic pedigree and published Cell2Sentence work give a head start, and benchmarks (BioSimBench, BioSimGym) could become a standard, but large labs and funded rivals pursue similar virtual cell models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell as of the batch (W26). Well funded peers were already building virtual cell and AI drug discovery platforms.

market_need_then: Pharma spends heavily on discovery and most candidates fail, so there is demand for computational screening. The company says it works with a top 10 pharma and signed a March 2026 MOU with Senhwa Biosciences (per a search summary, one source).

identity.visual_style: Minimal, spare layout with scientific credibility signals (Yale, ICML)
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, declarative, for example 'Simulate biology. Predict how your drugs work.'

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found beyond a CellType CLI Product Hunt listing and aggregator profiles.

brand_strength.rationale: Very new, minimal brand with a generic name; no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: CellType is an active W26 company with an academic founding team from Yale whose Cell2Sentence work underpins the product. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found. It is too early for an outcome; the main risks are the research difficulty and well funded rivals in AI drug discovery, while the strength is deep founder-market fit.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators disagree. PitchBook and CB Insights show about $500K total with a seed dated 2026-03-18 (investors named by one aggregator include Pioneer Fund and ACVC Partners); Caplight dates a seed 2026-01-01; StartupHub lists $12.0M which could not be confirmed. None recorded as a round. Competitors named in 2025 and 2026 coverage (GenBio AI, Recursion, Isomorphic) have no founding-dated source opened, so the list is empty. Note StartupHub gave San Francisco and 2023 which conflicts with YC (2025, New York).
